title: BACSAM-II sensible-heat-flux analysis (code)

creators.name: Müller, Joshua J.
creators.affiliation: Leipzig Institute for Meteorology (LIM), Leipzig University

description:
Code of J. J. Müller, I. Staudinger, F. Gebhardt, D. J. Simon, L. Köhler, J. Hartmann, A. Ehrlich, M. Schäfer, M. D. Shupe and M. Wendisch: Evaluation of reanalysis and satellite products of sensible heat flux over Arctic sea ice against airborne eddy-covariance measurements (submitted to Atmospheric Measurement Techniques).

The code reproduces every data-derived number, table and figure of the paper from the published data, which it downloads and checks: the measurements from PANGAEA (doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.995979, master tracks doi:10.1594/PANGAEA.971763) and every other input from the Zenodo data record doi:10.5281/zenodo.23729591. It computes the eddy-covariance sensible heat flux from the 100 Hz measurements of the T-Bird, a sensor package towed below the research aircraft Polar 6 during the BACSAM-II campaign (Svalbard, April 2024); bulk estimates driven by in situ, MODIS and ERA5 inputs; the model-diagnosed fluxes of ERA5 and CARRA; the sensitivity analysis and the uncertainty budget. With pixi run all, a locked Python environment recomputes them and compares every printed number with the committed reference expected_numbers.txt. README.md describes the procedure, AGENTS.md how to check a statement of the paper against the code, DATA.md the data files. The archive contains no data.

The code is released under the MIT License. The downloaded data remain under their own terms (CC BY 4.0 for the PANGAEA datasets and the Zenodo data record, whose third-party products keep the terms of their providers); see DATA.md.
